## Permanent vs. temporary code

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%" .fragment}
### Permanent code

Code needed to complete a task, e.g. make a map

e.g. `read_csv()` to load a dataset

<span style="color: #FFFFFF;">e.g. </span>`filter()` to filter rows

<span style="color: #FFFFFF;">e.g. </span>`hotspot_map()` to make a map
:::

::: {.column width="50%" .fragment}
### Temporary code

Code needed only to _develop_ the code needed to complete a task

e.g. `head(attacks)` to find column names

<span style="color: #FFFFFF;">e.g. </span>`check_code()` to check your code

<span style="color: #FFFFFF;">e.g. </span>`excel_sheets()` to find Excel sheet names
:::

::::

::: {.fragment}

  st_transform("EPSG:26967") |>

## :sunglasses: Comment your code


```{r}
#| label: draw-labelled-attacks-script
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "1, 3, 6"

# Map recorded fatal terrorist attacks in London from 2010 to 2018.

# Load packages
pacman::p_load(here, httr2, sf, sfhotspot, tidyverse)

# Download the original data and keep a local copy
request("https://mpjashby.github.io/crimemappingdata/london_attacks.csv") |>
  req_perform(path = here("data", "raw", "london_attacks.csv"))

# Read data
attacks <- read_csv(here("data", "raw", "london_attacks.csv"))

# Keep only records within the requested date range, including both ends
attacks_filtered <- filter(attacks, date >= "2010-01-01", date <= "2018-12-31")

# Convert longitude and latitude to a spatial object
attacks_sf <- st_as_sf(
  attacks_filtered,
  coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
  crs = "EPSG:4326"
)
```

## :wind_face: Let your code breathe

```{r}
#| label: show-spaced-map-script
#| eval: false

# Map recorded fatal terrorist attacks in London from 2010 to 2018.

# Load packages
pacman::p_load(here, httr2, sf, sfhotspot, tidyverse)

# Download the original data and keep a local copy
request("https://mpjashby.github.io/crimemappingdata/london_attacks.csv") |>
  req_perform(path = here("data", "raw", "london_attacks.csv"))

# Read data
attacks <- read_csv(here("data", "raw", "london_attacks.csv"))

# Keep only records within the requested date range, including both ends
attacks_filtered <- filter(attacks, date >= "2010-01-01", date <= "2018-12-31")

# Convert longitude and latitude to a spatial object
attacks_sf <- st_as_sf(
  attacks_filtered,
  coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
  crs = "EPSG:4326"
)
```

# The pipe operator `|>`


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


## Lots of R code looks like this

```{r}
#| label: count-robbery-weekdays-intermediate
#| eval: false

# Load robbery data
robbery1 <- read_csv(here("data", "raw", "san_francisco_robbery.csv"))

# Select only the columns we need
robbery2 <- select(robbery1, date_time)

# Filter only those offences that occurred in the first quarter of 2019
robbery3 <- filter(robbery2, as_date(date_time) <= ymd("2019-03-31"))

# Create a new weekday variable
robbery4 <- mutate(robbery3, weekday = wday(date_time, label = TRUE))

# Count how many offences occurred on each weekday
count(robbery4, weekday)
```


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


## Lots of R code looks like this

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "5"

# Load robbery data
robbery1 <- read_csv(here("data", "raw", "san_francisco_robbery.csv"))

# Select only the columns we need
robbery2 <- select(robbery1, date_time)

# Filter only those offences that occurred in the first quarter of 2019
robbery3 <- filter(robbery2, as_date(date_time) <= ymd("2019-03-31"))

# Create a new weekday variable
robbery4 <- mutate(robbery3, weekday = wday(date_time, label = TRUE))

# Count how many offences occurred on each weekday
count(robbery4, weekday)
```


::: {.top-space}
`robbery1` is (a) created, (b) used _once_, and (c) never used again
:::


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


## Lots of R code looks like this

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "2,5,8,11,14"

# Load robbery data
robbery1 <- read_csv(here("data", "raw", "san_francisco_robbery.csv"))

# Select only the columns we need
robbery2 <- select(robbery1, date_time)

# Filter only those offences that occurred in the first quarter of 2019
robbery3 <- filter(robbery2, as_date(date_time) <= ymd("2019-03-31"))

# Create a new weekday variable
robbery4 <- mutate(robbery3, weekday = wday(date_time, label = TRUE))

# Count how many offences occurred on each weekday
count(robbery4, weekday)
```


::: {.top-space}
The same is true with `robbery2`, `robbery3` and `robbery4`
:::


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


## :no_entry_sign: create + use _once_ + never use again 

Unnecessary objects:

::: {.fragment .top-space}
make code longer :arrow_forward: harder to read :arrow_forward: harder to understand
:::

::: {.fragment .top-space}
increase risk of typo errors, e.g.

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "3"

robbery3 <- filter(robbery2, as_date(date_time) <= ymd("2019-03-31"))

robbery4 <- mutate(robbary3, weekday = wday(date_time, label = TRUE))
```
:::

::: {.fragment .top-space}
make it easier to mix up objects, e.g.

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "5"

robbery2 <- select(robbery1, date_time)

robbery3 <- filter(robbery2, as_date(date_time) <= ymd("2019-03-31"))

robbery4 <- mutate(robbery2, weekday = wday(date_time, label = TRUE))
```
:::


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


## :sunglasses: Use the pipe operator `|>`

```{r}
#| filename: "Bad"
#| eval: false

robbery1 <- read_csv(here("data", "raw", "san_francisco_robbery.csv"))

robbery2 <- select(robbery1, date_time)
```

::: {.top-space}
Use this:

```{r}
#| filename: "Good"
#| eval: false

robbery_dates <- here("data", "raw", "san_francisco_robbery.csv") |>
  read_csv() |>
  select(date_time)
```
:::

::: {.top-space}
* guarantees code is run in the right order
* minimises likelihood of typos
* once you're used to it, makes code easier to read
:::



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


## :sunglasses: Use the pipe operator `|>`


```{r}
#| eval: false

robbery_dates <- here("data", "raw", "san_francisco_robbery.csv") |>
  read_csv() |>
  select(date_time)
```

::: {.incremental .nobullets}
* connect each function to the next with `|>`
* don't include first argument (e.g. `robbery2`) of functions inside the _pipeline_
* start a new line after each `|>`
* indent every line (except the first) by 2 spaces
* insert `|>` with {{< kbd Cmd-Shift-M >}} on Mac, {{< kbd Ctrl-Shift-M >}} on Windows
:::


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


## You might also see code with the _magrittr pipe_

`|>` is also known as the _base R pipe_

`%>%` is an older version contained in the magrittr package

both work fine!



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


## Keep extending the _pipeline_ until you have produced an object you need to keep

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "6"

robbery_wday_count <- here("data", "raw", "san_francisco_robbery.csv") |>
  read_csv() |>
  select(date_time) |>
  filter(as_date(date_time) <= ymd("2019-03-31")) |>
  mutate(weekday = wday(date_time, label = TRUE)) |>
  count(weekday)

gt::gt(robbery_wday_count)
```

```{r}

#| code-line-numbers: "1"

robbery_wday_count <- here("data", "raw", "san_francisco_robbery.csv") |>
  read_csv() |>
  select(date_time) |>
  filter(as_date(date_time) <= ymd("2019-03-31")) |>
  mutate(weekday = wday(date_time, label = TRUE)) |>
  count(weekday)
```

::: {.nobullets}
* "Specify the file location **and then**"

## :warning: Don't add a pipe `|>` to the final line

R will (in effect) ask 'and then _what_?'

```{r}
#| error: true
#| code-line-numbers: "5"

robbery_wday_count <- here("data", "raw", "san_francisco_robbery.csv") |>
  filter(as_date(date_time) <= ymd("2019-03-31")) |> 
  mutate(weekday = wday(date_time, label = TRUE)) |> 
  count(weekday) |> 
```


::: {.fragment}
```{r}
#| error: true
#| code-line-numbers: "5"

robbery_wday_count <- here("data", "raw", "san_francisco_robbery.csv") |>
  filter(as_date(date_time) <= ymd("2019-03-31")) |>
  mutate(weekday = wday(date_time, label = TRUE)) |>
  count(weekday) |>

  nrow(robbery_wday_count)
```
:::
